My rule doesn't flip a pick on this evidence, but this is your least-supported call.

Run the model on polls at face value and it returns about 69, close to your number. The dispute is one assumption. Independents have tended to run behind their polls: Orman 2014 by 12, McMullin 2022 by 3 to 5, Osborn 2024 by 4, though Walker 2014 ran 1 ahead. Applying that gives 90 for Ricketts, and ratings give 96. Four races are too few to overrule you, and Osborn lost by 6.7 in a far worse national environment than this one. But the evidence leans toward Ricketts above 71.
